title: GauRast: Enhancing GPU Triangle Rasterizers to Accelerate 3D Gaussian Splatting
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) requires significant computation, making real-time rendering infeasible on resource-constrained edge GPUs; prior acceleration via dedicated accelerators incurs high integration and hardware costs.
motivation: 3DGS is emerging as a high-quality 3D rendering method, but computational requirements prevent adoption on edge devices; reusing existing GPU rasterization hardware could enable efficient acceleration.
method: Enhances existing GPU rasterizer hardware (rather than building dedicated accelerator) to support 3DGS operations by recognizing algorithmic similarities with conventional graphics pipelines. Optimizes rasterizer datapath to handle Gaussian splatting primitive types and blending operations.
key_novelty: First GPU rasterizer enhancement for 3DGS that avoids dedicated accelerator costs by exploiting graphics pipeline similarities.
contributions: 23x speedup and 24x energy reduction in 3DGS processing
6x faster end-to-end original 3DGS (24 FPS), 4x for efficiency-improved pipeline (46 FPS)
Only 0.2% area overhead relative to entire SoC
limitations: Not discussed; applicability to other 3D rendering techniques unclear.
primary_theme: GPU rasterizer enhancement for 3D Gaussian splatting
